chunks.text: In 1932, Australia sent soldiers with machine guns to fight a war. Against birds. And the birds won.
After World War One, many veterans became wheat farmers in Western Australia.
Then thousands of emus showed up, eating and trampling their crops.
So the army sent Major Meredith, two soldiers, two machine guns, and ten thousand bullets.
In November, near a town called Campion, the battle began.
The emus scattered in every direction. Then one of the guns jammed.
They tried shooting from a truck, but the ground was too bumpy to aim.
Six days in, they had fired twenty-five hundred bullets. Some reports say only about fifty emus fell.
A bird expert later joked that the emus used guerrilla tactics.
The army pulled out, came back, then quit for good.
In the end, Meredith claimed nine hundred eighty-six emus. That's about ten bullets per bird.
The emus are still there. Follow for more weird history.
